claim: Lymphocyte numbers need to be quite tightly regulated.
source: Lymphocyte numbers need to be quite tightly regulated.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that reflects established scientific knowledge about lymphocyte homeostasis.

claim: It is generally assumed that lymphocyte production and lifespan increase homeostatically when lymphocyte numbers are low.
source: It is generally assumed that lymphocyte production and lifespan increase homeostatically when lymphocyte numbers are low and, vice versa, return to normal once cell numbers have normalized.
evidence: This statement describes a widely accepted concept in the field, referencing general scientific consensus.

claim: The concept that lymphocyte production and lifespan increase homeostatically when lymphocyte numbers are low is largely based on experiments in mice.
source: This widely accepted concept is largely based on experiments in mice, but is hardly investigated in vivo in humans.
evidence: The statement references the source of evidence for the homeostatic concept, indicating it comes from mouse studies.

claim: The concept that lymphocyte production and lifespan increase homeostatically when lymphocyte numbers are low is hardly investigated in vivo in humans.
source: This widely accepted concept is largely based on experiments in mice, but is hardly investigated in vivo in humans.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in human research, based on the authors' assessment of the literature.

claim: The production rates of most T- and B-cell subsets in autoHSCT-patients 0.5-1 year post-transplantation were two to eight times higher than in healthy controls.
source: We indeed found that the production rates of most T- and B-cell subsets in autoHSCT-patients were two to eight times higher than in healthy controls, but went hand in hand with a threefold to ninefold increase in cell loss rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cell loss rates in autoHSCT-patients 0.5-1 year post-transplantation were threefold to ninefold higher than in healthy controls.
source: We indeed found that the production rates of most T- and B-cell subsets in autoHSCT-patients were two to eight times higher than in healthy controls, but went hand in hand with a threefold to ninefold increase in cell loss rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by calculations based on deuterium labeling data and cell number measurements.

claim: Increased lymphocyte production and loss rates did not normalize when cell numbers did in autoHSCT patients.
source: Both rates also did not normalize when cell numbers did.
evidence: This is supported by longitudinal measurements of cell numbers and dynamics in the study.

claim: Increased lymphocyte production and loss rates occur even long after autoHSCT.
source: This shows that increased lymphocyte production and loss rates occur even long after autoHSCT and can persist in the face of apparently normal cell numbers.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the study's findings in patients 0.5-1 year post-transplantation.

claim: Increased lymphocyte production and loss rates can persist in the face of apparently normal cell numbers.
source: This shows that increased lymphocyte production and loss rates occur even long after autoHSCT and can persist in the face of apparently normal cell numbers.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the observation that CD8+ T-cells and naive B-cells had normalized numbers but still showed increased dynamics.

claim: Studies in rodents have shown that lymphocyte division and lifespan increase in response to severe lymphopenic conditions.
source: Indeed, studies in rodents have shown that lymphocyte division and lifespan increase in response to severe lymphopenic conditions (Freitas and Rocha, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Robust peripheral proliferation of T-cells occurs upon adoptive cell transfer into severely lymphocyte-depleted mice.
source: Robust peripheral proliferation of T-cells occurs both upon adoptive cell transfer into severely lymphocyte-depleted mice and in partially immune-depleted hosts in the absence of adoptive cell transfer, a phenomenon termed lymphopenia-induced proliferation (LIP) (Freitas and Rocha, 2000; Miller and Stutman, 1984; Bell et al., 1987; Neujahr et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Rapid proliferation and extended survival of B-cells occur after adoptive cell transfer into B-cell deficient hosts.
source: Similarly, rapid proliferation and extended survival of B-cells occur after adoptive cell transfer into B-cell deficient hosts and correlate with peripheral B-cell numbers (Gaudin et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Full recovery of the T-cell compartment following an autologous HSCT in humans is notoriously slow, often taking several years.
source: However, in humans full recovery of the T-cell compartment following an autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (autoHSCT) is notoriously slow, often taking several years (Heining et al., 2007; Ringhoffer et al., 2013; Bosch et al., 2012; Williams et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Severe lymphopenia arising after HSCT has been associated with increased proliferation of naive and memory T-cells based on elevated frequencies of Ki-67+ cells.
source: On the basis of elevated frequencies of Ki-67+ cells, severe lymphopenia arising after HSCT and lymphocyte-depleting treatments has been associated with increased proliferation of naive and memory T-cells (Jones et al., 2013; Bouvy et al., 2013; Hazenberg et al., 2002; Alho et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Elevated frequencies of Ki-67+ cells decline within 3-6 months after cell depletion, despite patients being still deeply lymphopenic.
source: However, elevated frequencies of Ki-67+ cells were shown to decline within 3–6 months after cell depletion, despite the fact that patients were still deeply lymphopenic (Bouvy et al., 2013; Hazenberg et al., 2002; Alho et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Increased T-cell proliferation rates after allogeneic HSCT correlate with the occurrence of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD).
source: Furthermore, increased T-cell proliferation rates after allogeneic HSCT have been shown to correlate with the occurrence of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and infectious-disease-related complications (Hazenberg et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Increased T-cell proliferation rates after allogeneic HSCT correlate with infectious-disease-related complications.
source: Furthermore, increased T-cell proliferation rates after allogeneic HSCT have been shown to correlate with the occurrence of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and infectious-disease-related complications (Hazenberg et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Six patients who received an autoHSCT for the treatment of hematologic malignancies were studied using in vivo deuterium labeling.
source: To elucidate whether lymphocyte production and death rates in humans are regulated in a density-dependent manner, we used in vivo deuterium labeling to quantify the production and loss rates of different T- and B-cell subsets in patients who received an autologous HSCT (autoHSCT), and had no signs of clinically manifested infections or GVHD.
evidence: This describes the study design and patient population.

claim: Twelve months after autoHSCT, absolute numbers of CD4+ T-cells in patients were lower than in healthy individuals.
source: Twelve months after autoHSCT, absolute numbers of CD4+ T-cells and memory and natural effector B-cells in these patients were still lower than in healthy individuals, while CD8+ T-cell and naive B-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy control (HC) values.
evidence: This is supported by cell count measurements presented in the study.

claim: Twelve months after autoHSCT, absolute numbers of memory B-cells in patients were lower than in healthy individuals.
source: Twelve months after autoHSCT, absolute numbers of CD4+ T-cells and memory and natural effector B-cells in these patients were still lower than in healthy individuals, while CD8+ T-cell and naive B-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy control (HC) values.
evidence: This is supported by cell count measurements presented in the study.

claim: Twelve months after autoHSCT, CD8+ T-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy control values.
source: Twelve months after autoHSCT, absolute numbers of CD4+ T-cells and memory and natural effector B-cells in these patients were still lower than in healthy individuals, while CD8+ T-cell and naive B-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy control (HC) values.
evidence: This is supported by cell count measurements presented in the study.

claim: Twelve months after autoHSCT, naive B-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy control values.
source: Twelve months after autoHSCT, absolute numbers of CD4+ T-cells and memory and natural effector B-cells in these patients were still lower than in healthy individuals, while CD8+ T-cell and naive B-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy control (HC) values.
evidence: This is supported by cell count measurements presented in the study.

claim: The production rates of most lymphocyte subsets in autoHSCT patients were significantly higher than in healthy individuals, even for subsets that had already reconstituted.
source: Deuterium labeling revealed that the production rates of most lymphocyte subsets, even those that had already reconstituted, were significantly higher in patients post-autoHSCT than in healthy individuals.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling.

claim: Increased rates of T- and B-cell production could only be reconciled with stable cell numbers if lymphocyte loss rates were also significantly increased.
source: These increased rates of T- and B-cell production could only be reconciled with the observed stable cell numbers over the study time if lymphocyte loss rates were also significantly increased.
evidence: This is an inference based on mathematical modeling of production rates and cell numbers.

claim: Patients were included in the study between 196 days and 420 days post-autoHSCT.
source: Patients were included in the study between 196 days and 420 days post-autoHSCT, received deuterated water (2H2O) for 6 weeks, and were followed for approximately 1 year after start of the labeling period (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the study timeline and is shown in Figure 1.

claim: Patients received deuterated water for 6 weeks.
source: Patients were included in the study between 196 days and 420 days post-autoHSCT, received deuterated water (2H2O) for 6 weeks, and were followed for approximately 1 year after start of the labeling period (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the labeling protocol used in the study.

claim: Patients were followed for approximately 1 year after start of the labeling period.
source: Patients were included in the study between 196 days and 420 days post-autoHSCT, received deuterated water (2H2O) for 6 weeks, and were followed for approximately 1 year after start of the labeling period (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the study follow-up duration.

claim: Patient B withdrew from the study 10 weeks after the start of 2H2O labeling due to infectious complications unrelated to participation in the study.
source: Patient B withdrew from the study 10 weeks after the start of 2H2O labeling due to infectious complications unrelated to participation in the study.
evidence: This describes a study event for one patient.

claim: All patients except Patient B had no complications that needed treatment during the study follow-up.
source: All other patients had no complications that needed treatment during the study follow-up, which was supported by C-reactive protein (CRP) levels in the normal range (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by clinical monitoring and CRP measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: CRP levels in patients were in the normal range during the study follow-up.
source: All other patients had no complications that needed treatment during the study follow-up, which was supported by C-reactive protein (CRP) levels in the normal range (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by CRP measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: The sub-optimal T-cell recovery observed in the peripheral blood of patients post-autoHSCT was largely due to the slow reconstitution of CD4+ T-cells.
source: The sub-optimal T-cell recovery observed in the peripheral blood of patients post-autoHSCT (Figure 3A) was largely due to the slow reconstitution of CD4+ T-cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 3.

claim: At the start of 2H2O labeling, CD8+ T-cell numbers had reached normal levels in most patients.
source: At the start of 2H2O labeling, CD8+ T-cell numbers had reached normal levels in most patients, whereas CD4+ T-cell numbers remained below normal levels even 1.5 years post-autoHSCT.
evidence: This is supported by cell count measurements in the study.

claim: CD4+ T-cell numbers remained below normal levels even 1.5 years post-autoHSCT.
source: At the start of 2H2O labeling, CD8+ T-cell numbers had reached normal levels in most patients, whereas CD4+ T-cell numbers remained below normal levels even 1.5 years post-autoHSCT.
evidence: This is supported by longitudinal cell count measurements.

claim: An inverse CD4:CD8 ratio was observed in all patients except for patient C.
source: This resulted in an inverse CD4:CD8 ratio in all patients except for patient C (Figure 3C), who experienced extremely slow CD8+ T-cell reconstitution (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by CD4:CD8 ratio measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Patient C experienced extremely slow CD8+ T-cell reconstitution.
source: This resulted in an inverse CD4:CD8 ratio in all patients except for patient C (Figure 3C), who experienced extremely slow CD8+ T-cell reconstitution (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by CD8+ T-cell count data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Naive CD4+ T-cell numbers remained below normal levels throughout the 2-year follow-up period.
source: Naive (CD45RO-CD27+) CD4+ T-cell numbers remained below normal levels throughout the 2-year follow-up period, whereas memory (CD45RO+) CD4+ T-cells reached the lower range of normal levels around 400 days post-autoHSCT (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by longitudinal cell count measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Memory CD4+ T-cells reached the lower range of normal levels around 400 days post-autoHSCT.
source: Naive (CD45RO-CD27+) CD4+ T-cell numbers remained below normal levels throughout the 2-year follow-up period, whereas memory (CD45RO+) CD4+ T-cells reached the lower range of normal levels around 400 days post-autoHSCT (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by longitudinal cell count measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Naive and memory CD8+ T-cell numbers were at normal or supra-normal levels at the start of the study in all patients except for patient C.
source: Naive and memory CD8+ T-cell numbers were at normal or supra-normal levels at the start of the study in all patients except for patient C (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Despite the CD4+ T-cell lymphopenia observed in patients, their plasma concentrations of IL-7 and IL-15 were in the range of those of healthy controls.
source: Despite the CD4+ T-cell lymphopenia observed in these patients, their plasma concentrations of IL-7 and IL-15 and several other cytokines were in the range of those of HCs (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by cytokine measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: The production rates of naive CD4+ T-cells were six times higher in patients than in controls.
source: We found that the production rates of naive and memory CD4+ T-cells were, respectively, six times and three times higher in patients than in controls.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling.

claim: The production rates of memory CD4+ T-cells were three times higher in patients than in controls.
source: We found that the production rates of naive and memory CD4+ T-cells were, respectively, six times and three times higher in patients than in controls.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling.

claim: The estimated production rates of naive CD8+ T-cells were approximately eight times higher in patients compared to controls.
source: For naive and memory CD8+ T-cells, the estimated production rates were approximately eight and four times higher in patients compared to controls (Figure 4B and Figure 4—source data 2), despite the fact that absolute CD8+ T-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy levels 12 months post-transplantation.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The estimated production rates of memory CD8+ T-cells were approximately four times higher in patients compared to controls.
source: For naive and memory CD8+ T-cells, the estimated production rates were approximately eight and four times higher in patients compared to controls (Figure 4B and Figure 4—source data 2), despite the fact that absolute CD8+ T-cell numbers had already recovered to healthy levels 12 months post-transplantation.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The fraction of Ki-67+ cells within the naive CD4+ T-cell pool was significantly higher in patients compared to controls.
source: The fraction of Ki-67+ cells within the naive CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell pools was significantly higher in patients compared to controls (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 expression measurements shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The fraction of Ki-67+ cells within the naive CD8+ T-cell pool was significantly higher in patients compared to controls.
source: The fraction of Ki-67+ cells within the naive CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell pools was significantly higher in patients compared to controls (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 expression measurements shown in Figure 5A.

claim: For memory T-cell subsets, the fraction of Ki-67+ cells of patients did not differ significantly from those of controls.
source: For the memory T-cell subsets, in contrast, the fraction of Ki-67+ cells of patients did not differ significantly from those of controls (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 expression measurements shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The increased production rates of memory CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells may occur due to an increased influx from naive T-cells into the memory compartment, rather than increased T-cell division within the memory T-cell pools.
source: This suggests that the increased production rates of memory CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells may occur due to an increased influx from naive T-cells into the memory compartment, rather than increased T-cell division within the memory T-cell pools.
evidence: This is an inference based on the discrepancy between deuterium labeling and Ki-67 data.

claim: The average TREC content of naive CD4+ T-cells in patients was approximately 10-fold higher than in aged controls.
source: The average TREC content of naive CD4+ T-cells in patients was approximately 10-fold higher than in aged controls, and not significantly different from that of young individuals and CB (Figure 5B), even though all but one of the patients were more than 50 years of age.
evidence: This is supported by TREC measurements shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The average TREC content of naive CD4+ T-cells in patients was not significantly different from that of young individuals and cord blood.
source: The average TREC content of naive CD4+ T-cells in patients was approximately 10-fold higher than in aged controls, and not significantly different from that of young individuals and CB (Figure 5B), even though all but one of the patients were more than 50 years of age.
evidence: This is supported by TREC measurements shown in Figure 5B.

claim: For naive CD8+ T-cells, the average TREC content in patients was in the range of young and aged controls.
source: For naive CD8+ T-cells, the average TREC content in patients was in the range of young and aged controls (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by TREC measurements shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The fraction of CD31+ cells within the naive CD4+ T-cell population was slightly higher in patients than in aged controls.
source: The fraction of CD31+ cells within the naive CD4+ T-cell population was slightly higher in patients than in aged controls and slightly lower than in young controls and CB (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by CD31 expression measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The fraction of CD31+ cells within the naive CD4+ T-cell population was slightly lower in patients than in young controls and cord blood.
source: The fraction of CD31+ cells within the naive CD4+ T-cell population was slightly higher in patients than in aged controls and slightly lower than in young controls and CB (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by CD31 expression measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The increased T-cell production rate post-HSCT is at least partially due to increased T-cell division for naive T-cells.
source: For naive T-cells, the combined Ki-67, TREC, and CD31 data suggest that the increased T-cell production rate post-HSCT is at least partially due to increased T-cell division.
evidence: This is an inference based on multiple measurements (Ki-67, TREC, CD31).

claim: By day 200 post-autoHSCT, total CD19+ B-cell numbers had already reached normal or even supra-normal levels.
source: Although total CD19+ B-cell numbers and naive (IgM+CD27-) B-cell numbers had already reached normal or even supra-normal levels by day 200 post-autoHSCT, Ig class-switched (IgM-CD27+) and IgM+ (IgM+CD27+) memory B-cell numbers in most patients were still below, or in the lower range of, those of HCs throughout the study period (Figure 6A and B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by B-cell count measurements shown in Figure 6.

claim: By day 200 post-autoHSCT, naive B-cell numbers had already reached normal or even supra-normal levels.
source: Although total CD19+ B-cell numbers and naive (IgM+CD27-) B-cell numbers had already reached normal or even supra-normal levels by day 200 post-autoHSCT, Ig class-switched (IgM-CD27+) and IgM+ (IgM+CD27+) memory B-cell numbers in most patients were still below, or in the lower range of, those of HCs throughout the study period (Figure 6A and B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by B-cell count measurements shown in Figure 6.

claim: Ig class-switched memory B-cell numbers in most patients were still below, or in the lower range of, those of healthy controls throughout the study period.
source: Although total CD19+ B-cell numbers and naive (IgM+CD27-) B-cell numbers had already reached normal or even supra-normal levels by day 200 post-autoHSCT, Ig class-switched (IgM-CD27+) and IgM+ (IgM+CD27+) memory B-cell numbers in most patients were still below, or in the lower range of, those of HCs throughout the study period (Figure 6A and B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by B-cell count measurements shown in Figure 6.

claim: IgM+ memory B-cell numbers in most patients were still below, or in the lower range of, those of healthy controls throughout the study period.
source: Although total CD19+ B-cell numbers and naive (IgM+CD27-) B-cell numbers had already reached normal or even supra-normal levels by day 200 post-autoHSCT, Ig class-switched (IgM-CD27+) and IgM+ (IgM+CD27+) memory B-cell numbers in most patients were still below, or in the lower range of, those of HCs throughout the study period (Figure 6A and B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by B-cell count measurements shown in Figure 6.

claim: The production rates of Ig switched-memory B-cells were 3.5 times higher than in controls.
source: The production rates of Ig switched-memory B-cells and IgM+ memory B-cells were 3.5 times and 5 times higher than in controls, respectively (Figure 7B and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The production rates of IgM+ memory B-cells were 5 times higher than in controls.
source: The production rates of Ig switched-memory B-cells and IgM+ memory B-cells were 3.5 times and 5 times higher than in controls, respectively (Figure 7B and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The production rate of naive B-cells remained significantly higher than in healthy controls.
source: Also the production rate of naive B-cells, a population that had already reconstituted to supra-normal levels, remained significantly higher than in HCs (Figure 7B, Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and mathematical modeling shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The percentages of dividing Ki-67+ cells within IgM+ memory B-cells were significantly higher in patients than in healthy individuals.
source: The percentages of dividing, that is, Ki-67+, cells within IgM+ and Ig class-switched memory B-cells were significantly higher in patients than in healthy individuals (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 expression measurements shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The percentages of dividing Ki-67+ cells within Ig class-switched memory B-cells were significantly higher in patients than in healthy individuals.
source: The percentages of dividing, that is, Ki-67+, cells within IgM+ and Ig class-switched memory B-cells were significantly higher in patients than in healthy individuals (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 expression measurements shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The fraction of Ki-67+ cells within the naive B-cell subset was similar between patients and controls.
source: In contrast, the fraction of Ki-67+ cells within the naive B-cell subset was similar between patients and controls (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 expression measurements shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The division history of the naive B-cell subsets in patients tended to be lower than in controls.
source: The division history (measured as number of cell divisions) of the naive B-cell subsets in patients tended to be lower than in controls (although not significantly), suggesting that the output of naive B-cells from the bone marrow rather than their peripheral proliferation rate was increased after autoHSCT (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by KREC measurements shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The output of naive B-cells from the bone marrow rather than their peripheral proliferation rate was increased after autoHSCT.
source: The division history (measured as number of cell divisions) of the naive B-cell subsets in patients tended to be lower than in controls (although not significantly), suggesting that the output of naive B-cells from the bone marrow rather than their peripheral proliferation rate was increased after autoHSCT (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is an inference based on KREC and Ki-67 data.

claim: For most T- and B-cell subsets, the average loss rate was approximately three to five times higher post-autoHSCT than in healthy individuals.
source: For most T- and B-cell subsets, the average loss rate was approximately three to five times higher post-autoHSCT than in healthy individuals (Figure 8 and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on calculations using production rates and cell number changes shown in Figure 8.

claim: For naive CD8+ T-cells the average loss rate was 9.5 times higher in patients than in healthy individuals.
source: For naive CD8+ T-cells the average loss rate was even 9.5 times higher in patients than in healthy individuals (Figure 8 and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on calculations using production rates and cell number changes shown in Figure 8.

claim: Naive T-cell production rates do not increase to compensate for the at least 10-fold declined thymic output in elderly individuals.
source: We have previously shown that naive T-cell production rates do not increase to compensate for the at least 10-fold declined thymic output in elderly individuals (Westera et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a reference to previous work by the authors.

claim: High frequencies of proliferating lymphocytes under severe conditions of lymphopenia in humans have been linked to immune activation and clinical events.
source: Under more severe conditions of lymphopenia in humans, high frequencies of proliferating lymphocytes have been observed, but these have been linked to immune activation and clinical events, for example, GVHD and opportunistic infections (Hazenberg et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The patients in the study had no signs of GVHD.
source: Our deuterium labeling study shows that in patients receiving an autoHSCT, in the absence of GVHD, clinically manifested infections, and transplantation-related complications, the production rates of most T- and B-cell subsets were significantly increased 12 months after transplantation.
evidence: This describes the patient selection criteria for the study.

claim: The patients in the study had no clinically manifested infections.
source: Our deuterium labeling study shows that in patients receiving an autoHSCT, in the absence of GVHD, clinically manifested infections, and transplantation-related complications, the production rates of most T- and B-cell subsets were significantly increased 12 months after transplantation.
evidence: This describes the patient selection criteria for the study.

claim: The patients in the study had no transplantation-related complications.
source: Our deuterium labeling study shows that in patients receiving an autoHSCT, in the absence of GVHD, clinically manifested infections, and transplantation-related complications, the production rates of most T- and B-cell subsets were significantly increased 12 months after transplantation.
evidence: This describes the patient selection criteria for the study.

claim: T- and B-cell production rates did not normalize when cell numbers did.
source: We did two additional observations, however, that suggested that these increased lymphocyte production rates post-autoHSCT were not simply reflecting a homeostatic response to low cell numbers. First, T- and B-cell production rates did not normalize when cell numbers did.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study's longitudinal measurements.

claim: Not only lymphocyte production but also lymphocyte loss rates were significantly increased post-autoHSCT.
source: Second, not only lymphocyte production but also lymphocyte loss rates were significantly increased post-autoHSCT.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study's calculations.

claim: The observed increased lymphocyte production rates post-autoHSCT could reflect an overrepresentation of young lymphocytes within the lymphocyte pool.
source: Alternatively, the observed increased lymphocyte production rates post-autoHSCT could reflect an overrepresentation of young lymphocytes within the lymphocyte pool, in analogy with lymphocytes in the developing immune system of children, where especially in the first year T-cells have relatively high proliferation rates (van Gent et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation offered by the authors, supported by a citation.

claim: In mice, newly generated naive and memory T-cells have higher production and loss rates than their established counterparts.
source: Likewise, in mice it has been shown that newly generated naive and memory T-cells have higher production and loss rates than their established counterparts (Gossel et al., 2017; Rane et al., 2018; Reynaldi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research in mice.

claim: The increased proliferation and loss rates observed post-autoHSCT may reflect HSCT-related complications.
source: Finally, despite the fact that the patients in our study were included up to 12 months post-transplantation and were selected on the basis of being in good health, we cannot exclude the possibility that the increased proliferation and loss rates observed post-autoHSCT may reflect HSCT-related complications, such as the impact of initial chemotherapy and conditioning-therapy or subclinical infections and inflammation, which may have gone unnoticed.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation offered by the authors.

claim: The increased lymphocyte production rates may have been a response to increased lymphocyte loss rates, which themselves may have been induced by the transplantation.
source: In fact, the increased lymphocyte production rates may even have been a response to increased lymphocyte loss rates, which themselves may have been induced by the transplantation.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation offered by the authors.

claim: Normalized cell numbers cannot be taken as an indication that homeostasis has been restored.
source: Whatever the underlying explanation, the ongoing dysregulation of lymphocyte dynamics in itself is an important observation. It shows that normalized cell numbers cannot be taken as an indication that homeostasis has been restored.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: The availability of pro-survival and anti-apoptotic factors, such as IL-7, typically increases during lymphopenia.
source: This concept is supported by the observation that the availability of pro-survival and anti-apoptotic factors, such as IL-7 (Ponchel et al., 2011; Barata et al., 2019; Lundström et al., 2012), typically increases during lymphopenia.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In the study cohort, there was no evidence for increased IL-7 plasma levels.
source: In our cohort, we found no evidence for increased lL-7 plasma levels, consistent with the observation that lymphocyte loss rates in these patients were not decreased.
evidence: This is supported by IL-7 measurements in the study.

claim: IL-7 production may be hampered by transplantation-related damage to stromal cells or intestinal epithelial cells.
source: A possible explanation could be that IL-7 production was hampered by transplantation-related damage to, for example, stromal cells or intestinal epithelial cells, which are an important source of IL-7 (Barata et al., 2019; Lundström et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation offered by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: Lymphocyte loss rates were up to 10-fold increased after autoHSCT.
source: We found that lymphocyte loss rates were up to 10-fold increased after autoHSCT.
evidence: This is based on calculations from the study data.

claim: The fraction of pro-apoptotic cells increases following transplantation.
source: Although in the current study we did not take into account markers of cell death, the estimated increased cell loss rates are in line with previous human studies on T-cell survival after allogenic HSCT, which consistently reported that the fraction of pro-apoptotic cells increases following transplantation (Alho et al., 2016; Brugnoni et al., 1999; Lin et al., 2000; Poulin et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Excessive lymphocyte differentiation and/or increased migration to the tissues would increase cell loss rates.
source: Although this suggests that intervention with lymphocyte survival after HSCT may aid lymphocyte reconstitution, other factors apart from increased cell death may have contributed to the loss of cells from the peripheral blood. Excessive lymphocyte differentiation and/or increased migration to the tissues would also increase cell loss rates.
evidence: This is a logical inference about factors that could contribute to cell loss.

claim: CD4+ T-cell numbers were below the normal range 12 months post-autoHSCT.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Bosch et al., 2012; Alho et al., 2016; Storek et al., 2008), we found that 12 months post-autoHSCT, CD4+ T-cell numbers were below the normal range while CD8+ T-cells recovered more rapidly.
evidence: This is supported by cell count measurements and citations to previous research.

claim: CD8+ T-cells recovered more rapidly than CD4+ T-cells after autoHSCT.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Bosch et al., 2012; Alho et al., 2016; Storek et al., 2008), we found that 12 months post-autoHSCT, CD4+ T-cell numbers were below the normal range while CD8+ T-cells recovered more rapidly.
evidence: This is supported by cell count measurements and citations to previous research.

claim: The average production rates of most T-cell subsets were significantly increased following autoHSCT.
source: Deuterium labeling in patients revealed that the average production rates of most T-cell subsets were significantly increased following autoHSCT.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments.

claim: The increase in T-cell production rates was especially evident for naive T-cells.
source: This increase was especially evident for naive T-cells.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments.

claim: The high percentage of Ki-67+ naive T-cells post-autoHSCT suggests that increased naive T-cell production is to a large extent explained by increased peripheral T-cell proliferation.
source: The high percentage of Ki-67+ naive T-cells post-autoHSCT suggests that increased naive T-cell production is to a large extent explained by increased peripheral T-cell proliferation.
evidence: This is an inference based on Ki-67 expression data.

claim: Memory T-cell production rates based on deuterium enrichment were higher in patients compared to controls.
source: Memory T-cell production rates based on deuterium enrichment were also higher in patients compared to controls, while Ki-67 expression suggested that memory CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell proliferation rates were not significantly increased 0.5–1 year after autoHSCT in line with previous reports (Malphettes et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and citations.

claim: Ki-67 expression suggested that memory CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell proliferation rates were not significantly increased 0.5-1 year after autoHSCT.
source: Memory T-cell production rates based on deuterium enrichment were also higher in patients compared to controls, while Ki-67 expression suggested that memory CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell proliferation rates were not significantly increased 0.5–1 year after autoHSCT in line with previous reports (Malphettes et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by Ki-67 measurements and citations.

claim: Ki-67, a snapshot marker, may be less sensitive to detect differences in T-cell proliferation than long-term in vivo deuterium labeling.
source: This seeming contradiction may be explained by the fact that Ki-67, a snapshot marker, may be less sensitive to detect differences in T-cell proliferation than long-term in vivo deuterium labeling.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy between Ki-67 and deuterium labeling results.

claim: The increased production rate of memory T-cells post-autoHSCT may be due to increased transition of naive T-cells into the memory T-cell population.
source: Alternatively, the increased production rate of memory T-cells post-autoHSCT may be due to increased transition of naive T-cells into the memory T-cell population.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation offered by the authors.

claim: In mice, naive T-cells adoptively transferred into immunodeficient animals can acquire a memory phenotype after antigen independent stimulation and division.
source: In line with this, in mice it has been demonstrated that naive T-cells adoptively transferred into immunodeficient animals can acquire a memory phenotype after antigen independent stimulation and division (Cho et al., 2000; Goldrath et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research in mice.

claim: Total daily lymphocyte production was as high as in healthy controls for naive CD4+ T-cells.
source: We found that total daily lymphocyte production was as high as in HCs for naive CD4+ T-cells and higher than in HCs for all other lymphocyte subsets, suggesting that the increased lymphocyte production rates post-autoHSCT truly reflected increased T-cell proliferation and/or an increased influx from another lymphocyte compartment.
evidence: This is based on calculations shown in Figure 3—source data 1 and Figure 4—source data 2.

claim: Total daily lymphocyte production was higher than in healthy controls for all lymphocyte subsets except naive CD4+ T-cells.
source: We found that total daily lymphocyte production was as high as in HCs for naive CD4+ T-cells and higher than in HCs for all other lymphocyte subsets, suggesting that the increased lymphocyte production rates post-autoHSCT truly reflected increased T-cell proliferation and/or an increased influx from another lymphocyte compartment.
evidence: This is based on calculations shown in Figure 3—source data 1 and Figure 4—source data 2.

claim: T-cells bearing TRECs may be overrepresented in the peripheral T-cell pool post-transplantation when cell numbers are low.
source: Although increased TREC contents at first sight seem suggestive for increased thymic output, T-cells bearing TRECs may in fact be overrepresented in the peripheral T-cell pool post-transplantation when cell numbers are low (Hazenberg et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The finding that the average TREC content of naive CD4+ T-cells following autoHSCT was higher than in age-matched controls implies that the thymus had become functional again within 12 months after intense conditioning for autoHSCT.
source: The finding that the average TREC content of naive CD4+ T-cells following autoHSCT was higher than in age-matched controls provides no evidence that thymic output following transplantation was higher than in HCs, but does imply that the thymus had become functional again within 12 months after intense conditioning for autoHSCT.
evidence: This is an inference based on TREC measurements.

claim: The difference in average TREC content between naive CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells may reflect differences in the degree of depletion of naive CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells.
source: The fact that the average TREC content of naive CD4+ T -cells, but not that of naive CD8+ T-cells, was higher in patients than in healthy individuals may reflect differences in the degree of depletion of naive CD4+ and CD8+ T -cells.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation offered by the authors.

claim: The difference in average TREC content between naive CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells might reflect differences in the way CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells are generated.
source: Alternatively, it might reflect differences in the way CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells are generated.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation offered by the authors.

claim: Repertoire analyses in patients receiving an autoHSCT for the treatment of autoimmune diseases have suggested that CD4+ T-cells largely arise de novo.
source: In support of the latter explanation, repertoire analyses in patients receiving an autoHSCT for the treatment of autoimmune diseases have suggested that CD4+ T-cells largely arise de novo, since most CD4+ T-cell clones post-autoHSCT were not present at baseline, while CD8+ T-cells mainly expand from cells that were already circulating pre-transplantation (Muraro et al., 2005; Muraro et al., 2014; Dubinsky et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CD8+ T-cells mainly expand from cells that were already circulating pre-transplantation.
source: In support of the latter explanation, repertoire analyses in patients receiving an autoHSCT for the treatment of autoimmune diseases have suggested that CD4+ T-cells largely arise de novo, since most CD4+ T-cell clones post-autoHSCT were not present at baseline, while CD8+ T-cells mainly expand from cells that were already circulating pre-transplantation (Muraro et al., 2005; Muraro et al., 2014; Dubinsky et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The delayed reconstitution of Ig class-switched and IgM+ memory B-cells has typically been attributed to treatment-related damage to secondary lymphoid organs.
source: The delayed reconstitution of Ig class-switched and IgM+ memory B-cells has typically been attributed to treatment-related damage to secondary lymphoid organs, which may hamper the formation of germinal centers essential for somatic hypermutation and isotype switching (Avanzini et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: For naive, Ig class-switched, and IgM+ memory B-cells, both production rates and cell loss rates were increased 12 months post-autoHSCT.
source: Also for naive, Ig class-switched, and IgM+ memory B-cells, we found that not only production rates but also cell loss rates were increased 12 months post-autoHSCT, further supporting our conclusion that increased lymphocyte production rates do not simply reflect a homeostatic response to low lymphocyte numbers.
evidence: This is supported by deuterium labeling experiments and calculations.

claim: Increased lymphocyte production rates do not simply reflect a homeostatic response to low lymphocyte numbers.
source: Also for naive, Ig class-switched, and IgM+ memory B-cells, we found that not only production rates but also cell loss rates were increased 12 months post-autoHSCT, further supporting our conclusion that increased lymphocyte production rates do not simply reflect a homeostatic response to low lymphocyte numbers.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Lymphocyte production rates are increased despite the slow reconstitution of lymphocytes in autoHSCT patients.
source: In brief, our findings show that despite the slow reconstitution of lymphocytes in autoHSCT patients, lymphocyte production rates are increased.
evidence: This summarizes a key finding from the study.

claim: The labeling period of autoHSCT patients was 3 weeks shorter than the labeling period used in healthy controls.
source: To reduce the study burden, the labeling period of autoHSCT patients was 3 weeks shorter than the labeling period we used in our previous study in HCs (Westera et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes a methodological difference between patient and control groups.

claim: Different labeling periods for autoHSCT patients and healthy controls should not affect the estimated dynamic parameters due to the use of the multi-exponential model.
source: Thanks to the use of the multi-exponential model, these different labeling periods for autoHSCT patients and HCs should not affect the estimated dynamic parameters (Westera et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous methodological work.

claim: Lymphocyte dynamics hardly change with age.
source: Since lymphocyte dynamics hardly change with age (Westera et al., 2015), the comparisons in our study should not be affected by the relatively small age differences between patients and HCs.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The average number of CD34+ cells transplanted was 5.03 × 10^6 cells/kg.
source: Patients received a non T-cell depleted graft; the average number of CD34+ cells transplanted was 5.03 × 106 cells/kg (median, 4.12; range, 1.82–12.38).
evidence: This describes a characteristic of the transplant procedure.

claim: CD31+CD4+ T-cells are enriched in recent thymic emigrants (RTEs).
source: We also measured CD31 expression on naive CD4+ T-cells, as CD31+CD4+ T-cells are known to be enriched in recent thymic emigrants (RTEs) (Kohler and Thiel, 2009; van den Broek et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.
